chunks: When Abu Amr Uthman ibn Sa'id died, his son Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Uthman stood in his place, by the designation of Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) upon him, and the designation of his father Uthman (peace be upon him) regarding the command of the Qaim (peace be upon him).

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far (title of Muhammad ibn Uthman)
key_terms.أَبُو عَمْرٍو: Abu Amr (title of Uthman ibn Sa'id)

ai.seo_question: Who succeeded Uthman ibn Sa'id as the representative of the Imam during the Occultation?
ai.summary: This passage highlights the hereditary succession within the Four Deputies (al-Nuwab al-Arba'ah), specifically the transition from Uthman ibn Sa'id to his son Muhammad ibn Uthman. The dual validation—explicit designation (nass) by Imam al-Hasan al-Askari and confirmation by the father—underscores the Shia doctrine of clear, unbroken lineage in the Imam's authority during the Minor Occultation. This continuity ensured the stability of religious guidance and legal interpretation as the community awaited the reappearance of the Mahdi.
